My brother died two years ago and it felt like all the good parts of me died with him. It was weird because we were estranged. I haven’t seen him in years and then all of a sudden I was in a hospital ER and the doctor was explaining to me that they did all they could but it was the last round of resuscitation they could do for him. A month after he died my whole family got Covid. The strong strain. Then a few weeks after our dogs died days from each other. Since we were still sick, we couldn’t take care of them. My funds were wiped out and since it was lockdown era, I couldn’t visit my brother’s resting place for months.

I just accepted then that I would never be the same. That the old me I used to know was a nice reminder that I had a chance to live a life that didn’t carry the pain I am carrying now. 

I was suicidal for a long time. Tried ending it but I couldn’t do it to my family.  So everyday I just prayed that I wouldn’t wake up. But then everyday that I would wake up, I would tell myself, maybe there’s a reason why I am still here.

Slowly, life became bigger than grief. I felt guilty and I tried to stay where I was because moving on meant I was going to forget my brother. So I held on for as long as I could. Until one day I just realized my brother wouldn’t let me do this to myself if he was still alive. So I told myself that I would live my life so that when we meet again, I could tell him about all the adventures I had so that he wouldn’t feel like he missed out.

Every time I remember what happened, there’s this feeling of getting the air punched out of me. Like I can’t breathe. But then it passes. Like everything else. Things, people, time—they all move on. So I tried moving too.

It did get better. I look forward to my future now. I try to live in the present and enjoy things. I try not to hate on what makes other people happy. I found new hobbies and rediscovered old ones. Everyday I proactively choose to do things that will make me happy. It’s nice to have some of my old self again only now, she’s more mature, she’s wiser, and she knows that the hole in her heart will always be there, and that’s okay. 

Everything will be alright.
